evidence: Gell. 11.2.5: vestīrī … in forō honestē mōs erat
Sen. Ep. 47.16: in forō et in cūriā
terms.comment: Where English says “at” of a place one is in, Latin says “in”: in forō, at the forum; in lūdō, at school; in balneīs, at the baths.

evidence: Plaut. Amph. 1020–1021b: Quis ad forēs est?
terms.comment: At the edge of a thing, beside it, not in it: ad forēs, at the door; ad portam, at the gate. Ad forum esse, be at the forum, is Plautus’ (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.5.3: suprēmō tē sōle domī, Torquāte, manēbō
terms.comment: As for “in”: names of towns and small islands, domus, rūs and humus take the locative (see in).

phrases.latin: heus, ecquis hīc est? ecquis hoc aperit ōstium? — Quis ad forēs est? — Ego sum.
phrases.english: Hey, is anybody here? Will somebody open this door? — Who’s at the door? — It’s me.

phrases.latin: ad portās major prope mulierum quam virōrum multitūdō stetit, aut suōrum aliquem aut nūntiōs dē iīs opperiēns
phrases.english: at the gates stood a crowd of women almost larger than the crowd of men, waiting for one of their own or for news of them

phrases.latin: vestīrī … in forō honestē mōs erat, domī quod satis erat
phrases.english: the custom was to dress decently at the forum, and at home as much as was enough

phrases.latin: nōn est … quod amīcum tantum in forō et in cūriā quaerās: sī dīligenter attenderis, et domī inveniēs
phrases.english: there is no reason to look for a friend only at the forum and in the senate house: if you look carefully, you will find one at home too

phrases.latin: suprēmō tē sōle domī, Torquāte, manēbō
phrases.english: I shall wait for you at home at sunset, Torquatus
